newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close lower on U.S. Midwest rain.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close lower on U.S. Midwest rain.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed lower on greater-than-expected rainfall over the weekend in the eastern U.S. growing region, traders said.
"It opened lower on weather but there was a lot of buying during the lower open," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Meteorologists early Monday said a storm system brought rain to much of the Midwest and that the moisture was beneficial to the dry crop areas of the eastern Midwest.
Trading was quiet before the release of another key government crop report. USDA at 0730 CDT Wednesday will release its September crop production report.
Trading is seen choppy before that data is made public.
"They're waiting for the report Wednesday and keeping an eye on an early frost," Kucha said. "But no one sees frost for at least 10 days or so."
Lower cash basis markets, signs of South American hedge selling and selling by a key commercial hit prices. Cargill Inc sold 4.5 million bushels of November, traders said.
Soybeans closed 6-1/4 cents per bushel lower to 3/4 higher, with September down 4-1/4 at $8.20.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 33,000, down from 45,658 Friday.

In soybean options, Smith Barney bought 1,000 November $7.25 puts and sold 1,000 November $7.50 puts at 4-1/2, the traders said. Cargill Investor Services sold 400 March $8.50 calls and sold 400 March $7.50 puts at 46-1/2 cents, the traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 20,000 contracts, down from 22,772 Friday.
